newsitem.title: USA: NYNEX plans new Manhattan area code in 1998.
newsitem.headline: NYNEX plans new Manhattan area code in 1998.

text.p: NYNEX Corp said Friday it plans to introduce a second area code to Manhattan, in 1998 because an increase in demand for phone numbers is squeezing capacity in the borough's 212 area code.
In addition, the 917 area code, which is used primarily for cellular phones and pagers in Manhattan and the other four boroughs in New York City, is expected to run out of numbers in 1999.
NYNEX plans to use 646 for the new area code in Manhattan for all services, including cellular phones and pagers.

"We are running out of numbers in the 212 area code because of the demand for additional telephone numbers from our business and residence customers in Manhattan and from the growing number of telephone companies that are offering local exchange service in competition with NYNEX," said Arnold Eckelman, NYNEX's executive vice president and group executive for New York.
"In the past four years, the demand for numbers in the 212 area code has more than tripled," Eckelman said.

NYNEX said it proposed three options to the New York Public Service Commission for implementing the new area code, but its report to the commission recommends an overlay program in which the new area code would be applied to the same geographic area served by the 212 area code.
Under this option, NYNEX said, no customers in Manhattan would have to change their current numbers or area code, although those ordering new lines would be given a new code.
But NYNEX said the overlay option is the least disruptive and least expensive and would provide the longest period before the supply of telephone numbers in Manhattan would run out again.
NYNEX said it will seek input from consumers and from other telephone companies that operate in New York. It said the Public Service Commission is expected to act by September 30.
